questions.question: Which describes the correct data flow in an IRIS Production?
questions.explanation: Data enters via Business Service, is processed/routed by Business Process, then sent out via Business Operation: BS → BP → BO.

questions.question: What is the base class for a custom Business Service?
questions.explanation: A custom Business Service extends Ens.BusinessService. The other classes are for BP (Ens.BusinessProcess) and BO (Ens.BusinessOperation).

questions.question: What is the entry-point method that IRIS calls when a Business Operation receives a message?
questions.explanation: OnMessage() is the entry point for a Business Operation. OnProcessInput() is for Business Services; OnRequest() is for Business Processes.

questions.question: What does the following code do inside a Business Process?

options.text: Creates a new instance of MyApp.BO.DatabaseWriter and calls it directly
Sends a fire-and-forget message — the BP continues immediately without waiting
Blocks the Business Process until MyApp.BO.DatabaseWriter returns a response
Starts the Production and routes all future messages to DatabaseWriter

questions.explanation: SendRequestSync blocks the caller (Business Process) until the target returns a response — use it when the result is needed to continue processing.

questions.question: If OnProcessInput() returns an error status in a Business Service that uses EnsLib.File.InboundAdapter, what does the adapter do?

options.text: Deletes the source file and logs a warning
Does NOT delete or acknowledge the source file — it will be reprocessed on the next poll
Moves the file to an error archive directory

questions.explanation: When OnProcessInput() returns an error, the inbound adapter will NOT delete/acknowledge the source data, so the file will be reprocessed on the next polling cycle. This enables automatic retry.

questions.question: In which scenarios should you prefer SendRequestAsync() over SendRequestSync() in a Business Process? (select all that apply)

options.text: When the downstream Business Operation's response is needed to decide the next routing step
When multiple Business Operations can be triggered in parallel without waiting for each result
When the next processing step does not depend on the downstream response
When the adapter requires a synchronous acknowledgment before the message is accepted

questions.explanation: Use SendRequestAsync when results are not immediately needed: parallel fanout (B) or fire-and-forget flows (C). Options A and D require a synchronous result.

questions.question: A BPL Business Process class automatically extends which base class?
questions.explanation: A BPL class automatically extends Ens.BusinessProcessBPL — IRIS generates this code from the XML diagram in the Business Process Designer.

questions.question: In a BPL diagram, what is the purpose of the sync activity?

options.text: Saves the current context object to the database
Sends a synchronous message to the next downstream target
Waits for all preceding async call activities to complete before the flow continues
Synchronizes the Production configuration with the Management Portal

questions.explanation: The sync activity pauses the BPL flow until all previously dispatched async call activities have returned, enabling parallel fan-out followed by a join point.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid activities that can be used in a BPL Business Process diagram? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Valid BPL activities include assign, foreach, call, if, and sync. transform is not a standalone BPL activity — transformation is done with assign or via an ObjectScript BP.

questions.question: Which of the following adapter classes are inbound adapters that can be used with a Business Service? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Inbound adapters: EnsLib.File.InboundAdapter, EnsLib.HTTP.InboundAdapter, and EnsLib.SQL.InboundAdapter. The OutboundAdapter variants (B, E) are used by Business Operations to send data out.

questions.question: What is the correct base class for a message that carries a request between Production components?
questions.explanation: Request messages extend Ens.Request; response messages extend Ens.Response. Using %Persistent directly or Ens.Message does not provide the required Production message infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Messages in an IRIS Production are true? (select all that apply)

options.text: Messages are persisted to the database
The target name in SendRequestSync must match the config name in the Production, not the class name
Messages extend either Ens.Request or Ens.Response
Messages are passed by reference in memory and are never written to disk
Failed messages can be retried automatically because they are stored in the database

questions.explanation: Messages are persisted (A), require matching config names as targets (B), extend Ens.Request/Ens.Response (C), and support automatic retry via stored data (E). Option D is false — messages ARE written to disk.
